column2: Course Description: Basic introduction to C++ and the concept of object-oriented programming techniques. Applications to scientific computation applied to numerical methods, linear algebra and differential equations. Grade is largely based on projects and presentations.Antirequisite(s): The former Applied Mathematics 4611F/G.Extra Information: 3 lecture hours.  Offered in alternate years with Applied Mathematics 4615F/G.

column1: APPLMATH 3811A - COMPLEX VARIABLES WITH APPLCTN
column2: Course Description: Functions of a complex variable, analytic functions, integration in the complex plane, Taylor and Laurent series, analytic continuation, Cauchy's theorem, evaluation of integrals using residue theory, applications to Laplace transforms, conformal mapping and its applications. Antirequisite(s): Mathematics 3124A/B.Extra Information: 3 lecture hours.

column1: APPLMATH 3813B - NONLINEAR ORDINARY DIFF EQS
column2: Course Description: Existence and uniqueness of solutions, phase space, singular points, stability, periodic attractors, Poincaré-Bendixson theorem, examples from physics, biology and engineering, frequency (phase) locking, parametric resonance, Floquet theory, stability of periodic solutions, strange attractors and chaos, Lyapunov exponents, chaos in nature, fractals. Extra Information: 3 lecture hours.

column1: APPLMATH 3815A - PARTIAL DIFFERENTL EQUATIONS I
column2: Course Description: Boundary value problems for Laplace, heat, and wave equations; derivation of equations; separation of variables; Fourier series; Sturm-Liouville Theory; eigenfunction expansions; cylindrical and spherical problems; Legendre and Bessel functions; spherical harmonics; Fourier and Laplace transforms. Extra Information: 3 lecture hours.

column1: APPLMATH 3911G - MODELLING AND SIMULATION
column2: Course Description: Basic principles of modelling and simulation, description and treatment of deterministic and random processes, computational methods and applications with emphasis on the use of computers. The course includes a major project. Antirequisite(s): Physics 3926F/G. Extra Information: 3 lecture hours, 1 laboratory hour.

column1: APPLMATH 4615F - INTRO TO APP COMPUTER ALGEBRA
column2: Course Description: Strengths and limitations of computer algebra systems (CAS); complexity of exact computations versus possible instability of numerical computations; selecta from Groebner bases, resultants, fractional derivatives, Risch integration algorithm, special functions including the Lambert W function. The emphasis is on preparing the student to use CAS in mathematics, science, and engineering. Extra Information: 3 lecture hours.

column1: APPLMATH 4617B - NUMERICAL SOLUTION, P.D.E.
column2: Course Description: Finite difference methods, stability analysis for time-dependent problems. Extra Information: 3 lecture hours. Offered in alternate years with Applied Mathematics 4613A/B.

column1: APPLMATH 4999Z - PROJECT
column2: Course Description: The student will work on a project under faculty supervision. The project may involve an extension, or more detailed coverage, of material presented in other courses. Credit for the course will involve a written as well as oral presentation.
